In Osaka, Yuki had been getting headaches for five weeks. She was waking at 3 a.m. with her heart racing about work. She told herself it was just a busy quarter.
Then one morning she couldn't remember a meeting she had led the day before. That frightened her.
She booked an appointment with her doctor for Thursday. And that afternoon, she asked her manager, Oskar, for fifteen minutes.
"I have four projects. I can't do all four well right now. I'd like to delay the website audit to next month and ask Kenji to take the vendor review. I can keep the other two."
Oskar looked at her list. "You should have told me sooner."
"I know. I thought asking would look like I wasn't committed."
"It looks like you're paying attention," he said. He moved the audit and spoke to Kenji that day.
On Thursday, the doctor listened carefully and asked her to come back in two weeks. Yuki left feeling lighter than she had in a month.

qa.q: How long had Yuki been getting headaches?
qa.a: For five weeks.

qa.q: Why did Yuki wait so long to ask for help?
qa.a: Yuki was afraid that asking would look like she wasn't committed.

qa.q: Which steps did Yuki take, and why were they sensible?
qa.a: Yuki asked to delay one project and share another, and booked a doctor's appointment, because the symptoms had lasted weeks and reducing load early prevents worse.

qa.q: How does Oskar see Yuki's request?
qa.a: Oskar sees it as responsible, telling her it shows she's paying attention and acting on it the same day.

grounding: Illustrates a worker who asks to delay and share tasks and sees a doctor when symptoms persist, treating reduced load as a sensible response.

At the higher secondary school in Thrissur, Asif taught physics to four sections, coached the quiz team and had just been given exam invigilation for the whole of March.
By mid-February, his lower back ached all the time and he was sleeping badly. He found himself dreading the staff room. He told himself real teachers push through.
One evening, grading papers at ten, he read the same answer three times. He put the pen down.
The next morning he asked to see the principal, Mrs Payal Menon. "Ma'am, I can't do all of March the way it is. Could the invigilation be shared with the new teachers? And can the quiz team pause until April?"
She looked at the roster. "Why didn't you ask in January?"
"I thought it would look like I wasn't coping."
"You're not coping. That's why you're asking." She split the invigilation that day.
That week Asif also saw a doctor about his back, who asked him to return if it didn't settle.

qa.q: Until when does Asif ask to pause the quiz team?
qa.a: Until April.

qa.q: How did Asif feel about the staff room by mid-February?
qa.a: Asif felt dread about it, worn down by the load and the constant back pain.

qa.q: What did Asif ask for, and why was it a sensible response?
qa.a: He asked to share invigilation and pause the quiz team, and saw a doctor, because reducing demand early is wiser than pushing through until something breaks.

qa.a: She sees it as honest and necessary, acting that day, while wishing he had asked sooner.

Francis

Jatin, you asked how I got through last spring without falling apart. Honestly, I nearly didn't. I, Binita, was running the school's exam timetable, coaching the debate team and covering a colleague's two classes. By March I had headaches every afternoon and was snapping at the children.
My first instinct was to push harder. Wake earlier, stay later. Instead, one Friday I wrote a list of everything I was doing and took it to my principal. I said, "I can do the timetable and my own classes well. I can't do all of this well." I asked if the debate team could go to Mr Pinto till May, and if the extra classes could be split.
She said yes to both. I was shocked. I'd expected her to think I wasn't committed.
The headaches didn't stop straight away, so I saw my doctor the next week too. By May I was sleeping again, and teaching properly.

qa.q: What did Binita take to the principal?
qa.a: A list of everything Binita was doing.

qa.q: Why was Binita shocked when the principal said yes?
qa.a: Binita had been afraid the principal would see the request as a lack of commitment, so the quick yes came as a relieved surprise.

qa.q: What made Binita's request effective?
qa.a: Binita brought a clear list, named what could be done well, and proposed specific changes: debate to Mr Pinto till May and the extra classes split.

qa.q: What might the principal have thought on seeing the list?
qa.a: The principal probably saw a teacher being honest about limits early, and judged that sharing the work was better than losing Binita's good teaching.

grounding: Shows a worn-down person asking to drop or share tasks and seeing a doctor when symptoms continue, instead of pushing harder.
